builder_evidence: Fuzzboxes documents the Harmonic Generator as a G. P. Electronics fuzz conceived around 1964, publicly available by late 1965/early 1966, with construction completed at the G. P. Electronics workshop. The same source reports multiple local and London sales outlets and testimony from Gerry Pope and others.
relationship_status: The later Baldwin-Burns Buzzaround relationship is historically important but not required for builder qualification. Treat the Buzzaround as a separate Baldwin-Burns product and map the copied-design relationship later.
recommended_treatment: Promote to verified builder census. This is a strong early British dirt-maker anchor despite the apparent loss of surviving original specimens.

builder_evidence: Fuzzboxes records Clifford Musical Supplies, Yorkshire, advertising fuzz boxes in 1966, but explicitly says the shop may have been supplied by a small builder or may simply have stocked another maker's product. There is no evidence that Clifford itself manufactured the fuzz units.
relationship_status: Retailer-versus-builder status is unresolved and the evidence does not clear the hard gate.
recommended_treatment: Do not promote as a builder. Preserve only as a historical retail/distribution lead for later relationship research.
